title: The Global Bond Rout
summary: Higher yields, fiscal transmission and energy income.
assessment: The rate decision and energy windfalls are verified. The central unresolved step is the leap from large public borrowing to an approximately stimulative net effect of rate hikes. EPD’s stated distribution-growth rate is overstated; its long-term income thesis and Bitcoin outlook remain open.

claims.reason: The official decision verifies the quarter-point increase. This is a realized observation within the prior scenario, not a fresh forecast win. The remaining 2026 meeting outcome is still open.

claims.claim: Rate hikes are approximately net stimulative now.
claims.reason: Comparing total government issuance with private lending does not establish the marginal response to a rate change. Repricing maturities, recipient spending propensities, credit demand, asset values, exchange rates and expectations all matter. The claimed net offset requires an estimated counterfactual, not an accounting comparison of flow sizes.

claims.reason: For unchanged cash balances earning a floating rate and unchanged fixed-rate debt payments, a rate increase raises nominal net interest income. This validates the personal example but cannot be generalized to the whole economy without measuring other households and firms.

claims.reason: Assets were about $6.748tn on September 23 and nearly unchanged on November 4. Earlier reserve-management purchases support the gradual-expansion regime, but funding Treasury deficits is not the same stated objective as maintaining ample reserves.

claims.claim: Domestic balance sheets must absorb residual issuance.
claims.reason: As an accounting identity, issuance not bought abroad must be held domestically. The claim that nonbank capacity is severely limited needs a demand model, and bank purchases are not automatically unconstrained money creation. Relative prices, saving flows and balance-sheet regulation affect all buyer groups.

claims.claim: Policy can contain a disorderly bond market.
claims.reason: Standing lending tools, outright purchases and shorter Treasury issuance provide options, but the report makes deployment conditional on disorder. Their effectiveness, legal scope, collateral constraints and inflation consequences differ; availability is not an unconditional yield guarantee.

evidence.title: Reserve management purchase announcement
evidence.finding: Purchases began December 12, 2025 to maintain ample reserves; initial monthly amount about $40 billion. Technical reserve supply does not itself establish a change in the interest-rate stance.

claims.reason: Shell’s net debt fell during the quarter, supporting an observed improvement. Permanence is too strong: future losses, acquisitions, dividends and buybacks can consume the cash. A one-time earnings gain raises cumulative resources but does not guarantee a lasting net-debt reduction.

coverage_note: Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.
framework_lessons: An accounting income channel is not a complete macroeconomic causal estimate.
Temporary profits can improve a balance sheet without guaranteeing permanence.
verification_limitations: Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
